status_summary: No executive order stating that religious employers may operate according to their beliefs despite general nondiscrimination laws was found. Executive Order 14202 (2025-02-06) created a Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias that is to review agency activity, including at Labor and the EEOC; Executive Order 14205 (2025-02-07) created the White House Faith Office and states that faith-based entities should be able to compete on an equal footing for federal funding; and Executive Order 14291 (2025-05-01) created a Religious Liberty Commission whose report is to consider the First Amendment rights of employers and employees. None contains the employer directive described, and none addresses employment nondiscrimination law.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14202 establishes a Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias within DOJ, to review agency activity including Labor and the EEOC and recommend remedial and legislative steps.
Executive Order 14205 establishes the White House Faith Office, which advises on reducing burdens on religious exercise and on faith-based groups' access to federal funding.
Executive Order 14291 establishes the Religious Liberty Commission, whose report is to consider the First Amendment rights of employers and employees.

The Religious Liberty Commission presented the President with a final draft report containing 12 recommendations (DOJ press release 26-713); none of the recommendations listed in the release addresses religious employers or federal contractors under nondiscrimination law, and the release does not mention Title VII.
